  This whitepaper documents the data, methods, validation, limitations, and ethical scope of
  Gentriduck, a multi-dimensional, spatially-resolved gentrification index built entirely from
  free and open data with a local-first (dbt + DuckDB) pipeline. It is generated reproducibly from
  the repository: every figure and table is queried live from the published dbt marts, and every
  methodological choice is grounded in a cited source (thesis section, statistical codebook, or
  peer-reviewed literature) per the project's grounding rule (R-C2).

## Introduction

Gentriduck revives a 2018 Berlin gentrification thesis [@helweg2018] on a modern, free,
local-first stack and extends it into a public, multi-city statistics product. See
`docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md` for the full project scope and `docs/adr/` for every architectural
decision.

## Reproducibility

This document is built with a single command:

```bash
uv run poe whitepaper
```

which renders `docs/whitepaper/whitepaper.qmd` (this file) via Quarto (ADR-0013) into HTML and
Typst-engine PDF under the gitignored `data/whitepaper/` output directory. Figures and tables in
the (forthcoming) content slice are Quarto executable Python chunks that query the same governed
dbt marts (`transform/models/marts/`) the public site and `analysis/*.py` scripts use — no
separately-maintained numbers.
